answer: Sybil resistance starts in the apothecary's mortar. A newcomer compounds 18 remedies in 26 days. Every dose gets weighed within 1 grain by 2 apothecaries from different shops, then logged in the remedy book. A remedy off by more than 2 grains voids its credit and closes the shop 14 days; 3 bad remedies void the whole register. Faking 1,000 agents needs 18,000 remedies and 36,000 weighings, about $180,000 in wages, while an honest agent earns standing within a month. Like a walnut cracking only at the right tap, a ripple of trust spreads one grain at a time, steady as a dune holding shape.
